scope: Model/editor review after rewriting the reading exchange around an actual book-club entry context; not an independent human or learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: Book club? establishes why Leo asks Do you read books?, the learner answers that question directly, and then asks it back instead of reciting an isolated textbook sentence.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian consistently distinguishes reading from having or wanting a book and keeps the support dialogue colloquial.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: read is the only new lexical target; the familiar book domain and known Do you ...? shape keep the learning delta explicit.

distractorQuality.evidence: The semantic contrast between read, have and want uses the same book domain, so errors diagnose verb meaning rather than unrelated vocabulary recognition.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: A short reading question is plausible at entry to an established book-club event and now has a concrete conversational reason.

difficultyFit.evidence: One new verb plus one familiar question pattern is appropriate at this point in A1, while frequency and tense remain explicitly out of scope.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: read appears in listening, reciprocal dialogue, question reconstruction, semantic contrast and a hidden natural answer without adding another noun domain.

transferQuality.evidence: The learner transfers the Do you ...? shape from have to read and then moves between asking the question and answering it.

overallCoherence.evidence: The continued Monday book-club story, target sense, reciprocal dialogue and all scored tasks support one reading-activity outcome.

learnerExperience.evidence: Static review only; the exchange is less textbook-like than before, but real learner timing, speech recognition and delayed retention are still unmeasured.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
The Lesson does not establish reading frequency, tense contrast or broader reading vocabulary.
Final ElevenLabs prosody and delayed retention remain unmeasured.
resolvedFindings: The previous context-light Do you read books? exchange now occurs at an actual book-club entry point.
The learner asks the reading question back, making the exchange reciprocal instead of one-directional textbook practice.
Final retrieval is now a natural answer to Do you read books? rather than an isolated sentence recital.
